knowledge_point.title: Identifying Augmented Matrices in Row Echelon Form

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following augmented matrices have coefficient matrices in row echelon form? Treat the final column of each augmented matrix as its constants column.

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A coefficient matrix, obtained by omitting the final column of its augmented matrix, is in row echelon form if it satisfies the following conditions:

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a nonzero row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the preceding nonzero row.

With that in mind, let's look at each matrix in turn.

- The coefficient matrix of $A$ is in row echelon form (both conditions are satisfied).

$$
A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}4 & 2 & 10 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 7 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 11 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

- The coefficient matrix of $B$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry in row $2$, column $3$ is in the same column as the leading entry in row $1$, column $3$ (condition II is violated).

$$
B=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}0 & 0 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & -8 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

- The coefficient matrix of $C$ is not in row echelon form since the leading entry in row $3$, column $2$ is to the left of the leading entry in row $2$, column $3$ (condition II is violated).

$$
C=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-9 & 9 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & -5 & 11 & -6\end{array}\right]
$$

Therefore, select $A$.

I. All the zero rows (rows with only zeros), if any, are placed at the *bottom* of the matrix.

II. Each leading entry of a nonzero row is in a column *to the right* of the leading entry of the preceding nonzero row.

$$

- The coefficient matrix of $B$ is not in row echelon form since coefficient row $1$ contains only zeros, but row $2$ is nonzero (condition I is violated).

$$
